children: is seeking shareholder approval for a new corporate structure that would give CEO Dario Amodei and his six co-founders a combined 50.1% of voting power, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the plans.
The arrangement would give the founders a special class of shares with control over most corporate matters, provided at least three of the seven co-founders retain a minimum number of shares.
The structure is modeled on the founder-control system used by Palantir Technologies.
The founders would not control the election of Anthropic's board members, according to the report.
The board has seven seats, one of which is currently vacant. Anthropic also plans to give employees a separate class of shares that could act as tie-breaker votes on some matters.
The changes come as Anthropic prepares for a potential initial public offering that could be among the largest on record.
